speaker: john_heminges
text: Will? John Heminges. From Aldermanbury, and all quiet here.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: John. Quiet here. What is the afternoon?

speaker: john_heminges
text: I have sent to Holywell and to Margery Pell. The— the yard will be thin, she says, and what there is will be 'prentices with nothing to do. I say we play. If we shut, the Mayor writes that we feared our own audience.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: We play. An old comedy. Nothing with a crowd in it, and nothing with a crown.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The Shrew. A wife tamed and a wager won, and no crowd, and no crown.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The flag goes up as usual.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Come by the fields, not by the gate, and bid Phillips and Pope come over by boat and not by the Bridge. I have sent that bid already. You need not cross to deliver it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I come by the fields. I will not go near the gate.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: What Fleming? There's a man from Norwich lodges here.

speaker: john_heminges
text: God keep the man from Norwich. And you.

speaker: john_heminges
text: One thing I heard on Thursday. The aldermen were already blaming stage-plays drawing prentices together.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the comedy is the right one. No crowd, and no crown, and the flag up. God keep you.

speaker: john_heminges
text: And you. Item, the flag. Item, the fields. Item, the boat. I have no second question.
